issue: Remote Code Execution (RCE) via Shell Command Injection
recommendation: Completely avoid executing commands via a shell interpreter (`sh -c` or `bash -c`) with string interpolation of remote hostnames, paths, or replica names. Instead, invoke the binaries (`ssh`, `btrfs`, `tee`) directly using `tokio::process::Command` and pass arguments as separate elements in an argv slice to prevent the shell from executing metacharacters.

issue: Undefined Behavior (UB) & Memory Corruption via Unsafe `simd_json::from_str` on Standard Strings
recommendation: Do not use `simd_json::from_str` inside an `unsafe` block on standard `String` values returned by `tokio::fs::read_to_string` because they lack the page-alignment and padding guarantees (`simd_json::PADDING`) required by `simd-json`'s SIMD-vectorized parsing routines. Parse using safe parsing alternatives or read data into a padded byte vector before invoking `simd_json::from_slice`.

issue: Schema-as-Code Violations: Untyped/Ad-Hoc JSON Audit Fields
recommendation: Transition data contracts away from unstructured `simd_json::OwnedValue` or arbitrary `HashMap` instances. Define strict, versioned schemas using Protocol Buffers (via `prost`) or OSCAL templates. This establishes a robust schema-as-code discipline and prevents audit log parse failures due to contract drift.

issue: Insecure Temporary File Generation with Predictable Names & Race Conditions
recommendation: Avoid hardcoding predictable temporary filenames like `.current.json.tmp` inside the subvolume directories. Use the `tempfile` crate (which is already a workspace dependency) to generate cryptographically random, collision-resistant temporary file paths.

issue: Lack of Backpressure and Memory Exhaustion Risk via Unbounded Channels
recommendation: Replace `tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver` with a bounded channel receiver (`tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver`). Under high control-plane event volumes, this ensures backpressure is propagated to producers rather than leading to Out-Of-Memory (OOM) panic conditions.
